## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components in loop1, combined with a parallel mask-scan loop2 for respawn merge, can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
Working set = 69·N; L1d spills at N≈949, L2 at N≈60787. At q=0.01, cost FALLS from N=10000 (7.39–8.85 ns/p) to N=100000 (5.94–8.67 ns/p), reflecting overhead amortization as the per-particle loop body dominates fixed dispatch costs. Past the L2→DRAM spill, cost stays FLAT: best ns/p is 5.94 at N=100000, 5.98 at N=1000000, 5.92 at N=10000000 — no knee at the L2 boundary. Death rate raises the floor without altering the N-shape: at q=0.5 the best ns/p holds ~10.3–10.9 across all N≥100000, still flat. The curve is death-rate-limited, not cache-limited.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 11.65 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 39% of the 29.9 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is compute/overhead-bound, never bandwidth-bound: at q=0.01 the profile shows 67.1% compute, 27.3% backend stall. Bandwidth falls with death rate: 11.65 GB/s (q=0.01) → 10.09 (q=0.1) → 8.39 (q=0.25) → 6.68 (q=0.5), all at large N. The transition is by death rate, not by N — the N-curve is flat at every q. At q=0.5, branch_flush reaches 20.9%, confirming the branchy respawn path, not memory, caps throughput.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the per-particle math. The compute loop (0x10004dab8+) is entirely scalar: `ldp s5, s6`, `ldp s7, s16`, `ldr s17`, `fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, `fcvtzs`, `fcmp`, `csel` — single-precision scalar ops processing one component at a time. The scatter is byte-granular: `ldrb w2, [x1]`, `add w2, w2, w12`, `csel`, `strb w2, [x1]`, repeated for three channels per pixel. The only vectorization is in the mask-scan loop (0x10004dd00+): `ldp q1, q0` loads 32 mask bytes, `orr.16b`, `ext.16b`, `orr.8b` reduce to a nonzero test — vectorized across particles, not across components. No gather (`ld1`) appears. The 37 `bl` calls to `spawn` and 37 `cbz` branches confirm the branchy per-particle respawn path. Scalar codegen with byte stores explains why bandwidth stalls at 39% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the hypothesis predicts auto-vectorization approaching the streaming ceiling, but the compiler emitted scalar-only particle math (`fadd s5`, `fmul s5`, no NEON) and byte-granular scatter stores (`strb`), capping achieved bandwidth at 11.65 GB/s = 39% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling even at q=0.01. Death rate raises the floor from 5.92 ns/p (q=0.01) to 10.78 ns/p (q=0.5) via branch_flush reaching 20.9%, but the N-curve is flat at every death rate, confirming the bottleneck is compute and branch overhead, not memory bandwidth.
